data.narrative:
Corintis is a Series A semiconductor company founded by Remco van Erp, Sam Harrison, and Elison Matioli, having raised $25M to date. The Chips & Semiconductors sector includes 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers such as SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, and Credo Semiconductor, though no narrow peer set of sufficient size exists at the same stage and valuation tier.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable method here. Using total raised ($25M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to later-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $50M. This methodology reflects observed progression patterns across the sector.

Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied: while the Semiconductors peer universe trades at a median P/S of 21.4x, Corintis's revenue is not disclosed, precluding revenue-based valuation. Peer-median analysis similarly lacks sufficient narrow comparables—only 2 same or adjacent-stage peers within the semiconductor space meet filter criteria, below the 3-point threshold for robust statistical inference.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $42M to $57M, with a $50M median. Key uncertainties include absence of revenue disclosure, limited visibility into the competitive positioning relative to the broader private semiconductor cohort, and reliance on a single applicable method. Validation would benefit from additional revenue or unit economics data.
